current.text: He is a bench player for Phoenix, behind Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Dillon Brooks and Miles Bridges.
Last season he played about 29 minutes a game overall, but only about 23 to 24 minutes once Booker, Green and Brooks were all healthy.
Booker, Green, Bridges and Brooks are expected to take most of the minutes and usage. That leaves little room for him, and one expert doubts that his larger role from last season is still there.
He only pays off if a guard or wing ahead of him gets hurt. If Green, Booker or Brooks misses time, he would start and play about 30 minutes. As a starter he would rank three tiers higher.
Experts say not to draft him at his ESPN rank of 100. They call that rank too high.
Josh expects him to finish around the 150th best player unless his role changes.
Ben thinks he should start over Jalen Green, but expects Phoenix to start Green.
He re-signed with Phoenix on a 4-year deal worth about 40 million USD.

durable.text: Ben rates him as a better three-point shooter, ball handler and defender than Jalen Green.

note: Both sites price him at 2 USD, at rank 116 on Yahoo and 100 on ESPN. That puts him at the edge of our 144-player pool, and the experts think his bench role is worth closer to rank 150. He is not worth more than a 1 USD end-of-draft flyer. Without a starting role, his 2.7 threes and 1.2 steals come with a weak 42 percent FG% on about 10 shots a game. Early in the season, watch the health of Booker, Jalen Green and Dillon Brooks: if one of them misses time, he moves into a 30-minute starting role and becomes a quick FAB pickup.
